The offending vehicle involved in this case is a scooty bearing registration no. DL- 3SDM-6632, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with Usha Rani vs . Rohit Kumar & Ors.

The case of petitioner, briefly stated, is that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, she was returning from duty to her residence by foot.

When she reached near Mohan Singh Market Red Light, Sector-5, R.K. Puram, New Delhi, all of a sudden, a scooty bearing registration No.
DL-3SDM-6632 came from behind and hit her with great force due to which she fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
It is further stated that the petitioner was removed to JPNA Trauma Centre, where her MLC was prepared.
3. Respondent no. 1 and respondent no. 2 have not filed any reply/written statement to the DAR.
4. The respondent no. 3/Insurance Company had filed legal offer for a sum of Rs. 65,000/- plus actual medical bills, for settlement, which was not acceptable to the petitioner.

Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3 . Relief.
6. It is pertinent to mention that the petitioner had not suffered any physical permanent disability due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

Advocate for respondent no.3/Insurance Company.
The case record has also been perused.
It is pertinent to mention that R-1 and R-2 were proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 22.11.2022.
The finding on the aforesaid issues is reproduced in succeeding paragraphs hereinafter.

Whether the injured Smt. Usha Rani sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 22.12.2017, at about 05.15 pm, Near Mohan Singh Market Red Light, Sector-5, R.K. Puram, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-3SDM-6632 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

In order to prove negligence of respondent no. 1, the petitioner has examined herself as PW-1 and has filed her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW-1/A wherein he has narrated the mode and manner of accident and placed reliance on DAR as Ex. PW1/4 (colly).

During cross-examination, PW1 deposed that the scooty came from behind and hit her on the footpath.
She further deposed that the driver of scooty ran away, but she caught the pillion rider along with the scooty.
No effective cross examination regarding negligence has been led on behalf of the respondents.
9. It is explicit form the testimony of PW-1 that occurrence of accident has not been disputed and the testimony of the witness in this regard has gone unrebutted.
Nothing material could be elicited from the cross-examination of PW-1 to disbelieve or discard her testimony.
The testimony of PW-1 has been duly corroborated with the DAR filed by the IO as Ex. PW1/4 (colly).

Moreover, it has not been disputed that respondent no. 1 has been charge-sheeted in the aforesaid FIR for offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC for rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle negligently and rashly.

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.
10. Pertinently, Respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.

Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
12.

sentences.text: 14. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343) has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to petitioner is assessed hereinafter under the following heads:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 16.
The petitioner in her affidavit Ex. PW1/A has tendered on record her medical papers and bills as Ex. PW1/1 (colly) and discharge summary as Ex. PW1/2 (colly).
As per discharge summary of JPNA Trauma Centre which is part of Ex. PW1/1 (colly), the petitioner was admitted in the said hospital on 22.12.2017 and was discharged on the same day.

The discharge summary of AIIMS Hospital Ex.
PW1/2 (colly) further reveals that the petitioner was admitted in the said hospital on 26.12.2017 and was discharged on 29.12.2017.

The petitioner was diagnosed with fracture of right parasymphysis of mandible and left subcondyle of mandible and had undergone ORIF at the right parasymphisis region and conservative management of left subcondylar fracture under GA.

sentences.text: The petitioner has tendered on record her medical bills as Ex. PW1/1 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 30,150/-.
During cross examination, she denied the suggestion that the bills and medical treatment records are forged and fabricated and not related to the present accident.
She deposed that she has no other medical bills or payment receipts except the medical bills filed on record by her.
Needless to say, the insurance company has not led any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that she spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that she has spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, she is held entitled to Rs. 30,150/- towards her medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of actual earnings 18.
The petitioner has claimed in her affidavit Ex. PW1/A that she is working with CPWD.

The petitioner has tendered on record attested copies of her salary slips for the months of December,
2017 and January, 2018 as Ex. PW1/3 (colly), as per which the petitioner was working as Multi Tasking Staff with CPWD and was earning Rs. 38,430/- per month.

Hence, from the salary slips Ex.
PW1/3 (colly), it stands established on record that the petitioner was working as Multi Tasking Staff with CPWD and was earning Rs. 38,430/- per month.

19. In order to prove the leaves availed by her, the petitioner has examined on record PW2 Sh.
Pradeep Singh Bisht, Record Keeper/UDC from her office who has brought the leave record of petitioner as Ex. PW2/A (colly).
During cross examination, he deposed that the petitioner had availed medical leaves for 28 days, w.e.f. 26.12.2017 to 22.01.2018.

Perusal of Ex. PW2/A (colly)
reveals that the petitioner had availed earned leave for two days, i.e. 23.12.2017 and 23.01.2018 and medical leaves w.e.f. 26.12.2017 to 22.01.2018.
20.

The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has considered the said aspect in MAC App 812/2011 titled as Ramveer Singh Vs Rajesh Kumar and ors decided on 30.11.2012 wherein it has been observed as:-
"LOSS OF LEAVE:
6.

sentences.text: From the certificate Ex.PW1/4, it was established that the Appellant was on leave from 16.12.2007(the date of the accident) to 16.04.2009, that is, for a period of about 16 months.
He was again on leave for one month from 14.12.2009 to 14.01.2010 which was proved by the certificate Ex.PW1/5.

The Claims Tribunal instead of granting compensation on account of actual loss of leave, granted a lumpsum compensation of Rs. 50,000/- on the ground that the Appellant was paid salary during this period.
A victim of a motor vehicle accident cannot be made to suffer loss of his full pay leave or the medical leave for the benefit of the tortfeasor.
An employee loses an opportunity for encashment of leave at the time of his superannuation if the leaves are exhausted during service.
In the circumstances, the Appellant is entitled to Usha Rani vs . Rohit Kumar & Ors.

sentences.text: It is thus amply clear from the reading of aforesaid judgments that the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for leaves availed by him due to accident irrespective of the nature of leaves.
21. It is evident from the testimonies of PW-2 coupled with aforesaid exhibited documents that the petitioner had availed leaves for 30 days due to the accident.
Therefore, under this head, she is being awarded an amount of Rs. 38,430/-, i.e. one month salary under this head.
(iii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities.
22. As stated above, the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries in the accident.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate her for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which she had actually suffered because of the above injuries and disability, but an effort has to be made to compensate her for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.25,000/- each is being awarded to her towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.
Further, an amount of Rs.10,000/- is also awarded to her towards the loss of amenities suffered by her during treatment.
Thus, she is awarded total amount of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
(iv) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 23.
The petitioner in her affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that she had spent Rs. 35,400/- towards conveyance and Rs. 3,10,680/- for special diet.
However, she has not filed any document in order to substantiate her above claim.

Still, this tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for petitioner for frequently visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with her treatment and special diet for her early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Hence, an amount of Rs. 20,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance and special diet.
However, no amount is being awarded to the petitioner towards attendant charges.

Therefore,
a total amount of Rs.40,000/- is being awarded to her under this head.
Issue No.3/Relief 24.
In view of foregoing discussion, the petitioner is thus awarded a sum of Rs. 1,68,580/- (

Rs.
30,150/- + Rs. 38,430/- + Rs. 60,000/- + Rs. 40,000/-) (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Eight Thousand Five Hundred Eighty only) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR
. However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Nothing material could be elicited from the cross-examination of PW-1 to disbelieve or discard her testimony.
The testimony of PW-1 has been duly corroborated with the DAR filed by the IO as Ex. PW1/4 (colly).
Moreover, it has not been disputed that respondent no. 1 has been charge-sheeted in the aforesaid FIR for offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC for rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle negligently and rashly.
Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
11.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
12.
14. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
Usha Rani vs . Rohit Kumar & Ors. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106690778/
4 17.
In the circumstances, the Appellant is entitled to Usha Rani vs . Rohit Kumar & Ors.
Similar view was taken by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the judgment dated 04.09.2012 passed in MAC App.
No.215/2010, Sandeep Mishra Vs. Ajay Kumar Yadav & Ors.
It is thus amply clear from the reading of aforesaid judgments that the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for leaves availed by him due to accident irrespective of the nature of leaves.
